sights.w: The only publicly open part of Apple's ring-shaped 'spaceship' campus, with an Apple Store, cafe, roof terrace overlooking the ring, and an augmented-reality model of Apple Park.
sights.k: The HQ itself is closed to the public; only the Visitor Center (store, cafe, AR model, rooftop terrace) is open. Open daily. Open to visitors.
sources: Apple opens new visitor center in Cupertino — https://abc7news.com/post/apple-opens-new-visitor-center-in-cupertino/2662716/
Aerial Photos Show New Apple 'Spaceship' Campus Taking Shape in Cupertino — https://nbcbayarea.com/news/tech/Aerial-Photos-Show-New-Apple-Spaceship-Campus-Taking-Shape-in-Cupertino-257432561.html

sights.address: 1401 N Shoreline Blvd, Mountain View, CA 94043
sights.w: The world's largest collection tracing the history of computing, from ancient abacuses and a working Babbage Difference Engine to the PDP-1, Cray supercomputers, and a restored self-driving Google car.
sights.k: Closed Mondays and Tuesdays; open Wed-Sun 10am-5pm. Open to visitors.

sights.address: 201 S Market St, San Jose, CA 95113
sights.w: A hands-on science and technology center in downtown San Jose with interactive innovation labs, a design workshop, and an IMAX dome theater, aimed at families and curious minds.
sights.k: Since June 2026 on a reduced schedule; closed Mondays and Tuesdays. Not permanently closed despite some stale listings. Open to visitors.

sights.address: 2200 Mission College Blvd, Santa Clara, CA 95054
sights.w: A free museum inside Intel's Santa Clara headquarters telling the story of the microprocessor and how silicon chips are designed and manufactured, from sand to wafer.
sights.k: Free admission; open weekdays only (roughly 9am-5pm). Call ahead as it occasionally closes for corporate events. Open to visitors.

sights.n: HP Garage - Birthplace of Silicon Valley
sights.w: The modest one-car garage where Bill Hewlett and Dave Packard started Hewlett-Packard in 1938, designated California Historical Landmark No. 976 and widely called the birthplace of Silicon Valley.
sights.k: Private property and not open for tours; view and photograph the garage and plaque from the public sidewalk only. Viewable from the street/sidewalk only — no public interior access.

sights.w: The sandstone Romanesque heart of Stanford's campus, where the arcaded Main Quad frames Memorial Church, famed for its gold-leaf mosaic facade and stained glass, built by Jane Stanford in memory of Leland.
sights.k: Free and open to the public; the Quad is walkable any time and the church is open daily outside services. Docent tours Fridays.

sights.w: Stanford's 285-foot landmark tower, home to the Hoover Institution archives, with a 14th-floor observation deck giving sweeping views over campus and across Silicon Valley to the bay.
sights.k: Observation deck is ticketed and keeps seasonal hours - it closes for parts of the year (e.g. mid-Aug 2026 through late Jan 2027), so verify before visiting.

sights.n: Cantor Arts Center & Rodin Sculpture Garden
sights.w: Stanford's free art museum spanning 5,000 years, holding the largest Rodin collection outside Paris - including a cast of The Gates of Hell - with an outdoor Rodin Sculpture Garden open around the clock.
sights.k: Free admission; museum closed Tuesdays. The outdoor sculpture garden is open 24/7 and lit at night.

sights.w: A jewel-box museum of postwar American modern and contemporary art - Pollock, Rothko, Diebenkorn, de Kooning - given to Stanford by the Anderson family, next door to the Cantor Arts Center.
sights.k: Always free; open Thursday-Monday, closed Tuesday and Wednesday. No reservation needed.

sights.w: Stanford's acoustically acclaimed 842-seat 'vineyard'-style concert hall, opened in 2013, where audience terraces wrap the stage so no seat sits more than 75 feet from the performers.
sights.k: A performing-arts venue - visitable by attending a Stanford Live concert or event; check the calendar for public performances.

sights.address: 525 S Winchester Blvd, San Jose, CA 95128
sights.w: The sprawling, labyrinthine Victorian mansion built continuously for decades by rifle heiress Sarah Winchester, riddled with stairs to nowhere, doors opening onto walls, and 160 rooms.
sights.k: Guided tours only, by ticket; open daily. On the National Register of Historic Places.

sights.w: The largest collection of Egyptian antiquities on display in western North America - mummies, sarcophagi, amulets, and a walk-in replica rock-cut tomb - set in a distinctive Egyptian-Revival campus.
sights.k: Ticketed; check days open before visiting. Free parking at Naglee Ave and Chapman St, one block east.

sights.address: 500 El Camino Real, Santa Clara, CA 95053
sights.w: The eighth of California's 21 Franciscan missions, founded in 1777 and now the centerpiece of Santa Clara University, with a restored adobe-style church, rose gardens, and centuries-old olive trees.
sights.k: Free; grounds and church open daily roughly 7am-7pm. No guided tours (self-guided pamphlet available). Free visitor parking permit at the campus kiosk on weekdays.

sights.address: 80 S Market St, San Jose, CA 95113
sights.w: San Jose's landmark downtown cathedral, an 1877 Italianate-Renaissance church crowned by a great dome, richly frescoed inside and designated a minor basilica by the Vatican.
sights.k: Free to visit outside of Mass and services; open to the public in downtown San Jose.

sights.w: A 14-acre open-air museum in Kelley Park with 30-plus original and re-created homes, shops, and landmarks of early San Jose - including a half-scale Electric Light Tower - plus a working trolley and the O'Brien's ice cream parlor.
sights.k: Park grounds free to walk; some buildings and the trolley run on limited days. Run by History San Jose.
